Name of the Surah

• It is called "an-Nisa' (The Women)", because the rulings concerning women in it are more numerous than in other surahs.

Among the Objectives of the Surah

• Commanding people to be mindful of God (taqwa), and reminding them that they were created from a single soul. Implicit in this is the instruction regarding proper conduct among them: maintaining ties of kinship, and dealing kindly with the weak among people, such as women and orphans, and giving due regard to those who hold rights.

• Explaining a number of rulings concerning women: such as the command to observe their rights, to establish justice in dealing with them, and reference to the contracts of marriage (nikah) and the bridal gift (sadaq), the manner of dealing with women in both states of uprightness and deviation, living with them (mu'ashara), the mention of those women who are forbidden (in marriage), and the rulings concerning slave-girls possessed by right-hand ownership (milk al-yamin).

• Explaining a number of other legal rulings: such as the command to care for orphans and to safeguard their property, the division of inheritance, the groundwork for the prohibition of drinking wine (khamr), and a group of rulings on purity (taharah) and prayer (salah).

• Urging social solidarity, represented in kindness to parents, maintaining ties of kinship, and other matters, and explaining that kindness is the foundation of internal reform, and that the foundation of kindness is mutual support (takaful) and compassion (tarahum), trustworthiness (amanah) and justice, so that society may be firmly built.

• Pointing to external reform, and that the stability of the Ummah depends upon it, through jihad to repel the harm of the polytheists; and mentioning some principles of the dealings between the state of the Muslims and other states; and commanding caution against enemies within, since the command to fight is followed by discussion of the hypocrites (munafiqun) and their danger.

• Explaining the rulings on transactions among the community of Muslims concerning property and blood, and establishing the legal ruling among Muslims regarding rights and the defense of the one who is wronged.

• Warning against the misguidance of the People of the Book and their attitude toward the noble messengers of God, and explaining the misguidance of the Christians concerning Jesus son of Mary, as they exaggerated regarding him and his mother, to the point that they worshipped them besides God, and invented the doctrine of "Trinity" (tathlith); and concluding this with a call to return to the correct belief.

[Tafsir]

O people, fear God and adhere to His commands, and avoid His prohibitions; for it is He who created you from a single soul, which is Adam (peace be upon him), and created from it its spouse, who is Eve, and dispersed from the two of them many men and many women throughout the regions of the earth. Be mindful of God, by whom you ask one another, and beware of severing your ties of kinship. Indeed, God is ever watchful over all your conditions.

Give the orphans their property once they reach the age of maturity, those whose fathers have died while they were still below the age of puberty, and you were their guardians. And when you perceive in them the ability to safeguard their property, do not take the good of their property and substitute in its place the bad of your own property, and do not mix their property with yours so that you may thereby devour their property by deceit. Indeed, whoever dares to do that has committed a great sin.

If you fear that you will not act justly toward orphan girls under your guardianship, then do not give them their dowries as you would give to others; instead, leave them and marry from other women whatever seems good to you: two, three, or four. But if you fear that you will not be equitable among them, then be content with one, or with what your right hand possesses of slave women. That which I have prescribed for you regarding orphan girls, and marrying from one to four, or limiting yourselves to one or to what your right hand possesses, is closer to avoiding injustice and transgression.

And give women (O husbands) their bridal gifts (mahr) as a free gift, an obligation and a binding duty, given willingly from yourselves. But if they are pleased to give you back some of it willingly, then take it and make use of it, for it is lawful and wholesome.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 5:

Do not give, O guardians, those who squander among men, women and children their wealth that is in your hands, so that they place it in other than its proper use. For this wealth is that upon which the lives of people depend. Provide for them from it and clothe them, and speak to them a kind word of good speech and good manners.

Test the orphans under your care to ascertain their ability to manage their property well. When they reach the age of maturity, and you perceive in them sound judgment in their religion and capability in preserving their wealth, then hand their property over to them. Do not misappropriate it by spending it wastefully or in other than its proper places, nor hasten to consume it before they grow up and claim it from you. Whoever among you is wealthy should abstain from taking from the orphan's property, and whoever is poor may take from it according to his need when necessity requires. When you know that they are able to preserve their property after reaching maturity, and you have handed it over to them, then call witnesses against them, to guarantee that their rights reach them in full and so that they cannot deny it. It is sufficient for you that Allah is a witness over you and will hold you accountable for what you have done.

For males, whether young or old, there is a share that Allah has prescribed from what the parents and close relatives leave behind of wealth, whether little or much, in specified and clear portions that Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, has obligated for these heirs; and likewise for females.

When the division of the inheritance is taking place, if relatives of the deceased who have no share in the estate are present, or those whose fathers died while they were still children below the age of puberty, or those who do not own what suffices them and meets their needs, then give them something of the wealth, as a recommended act, before the estate is divided among its rightful heirs. And speak to them with good words, neither harsh nor ugly.

Let those who would leave behind them weak, young children, fearing for them, be fearful (of wronging orphans). So let them be mindful of God regarding those under their care of orphans and others, by preserving their wealth, raising them well, warding off harm from them, and let them speak to them words that are in accordance with justice and kindness.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 10:

Indeed, those who wrongfully devour the wealth of orphans, taking it without right, are only consuming a fire that blazes in their bellies on the Day of Resurrection, and they will enter a Fire whose heat they will suffer.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 11:

﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children: when one of you dies and leaves children, male and female, his whole estate goes to them, the male receiving the equal of the share of two females, if there is no other heir besides them. If they leave only daughters, two or more, they receive two-thirds of what the deceased left; and if there is one daughter, she receives half. As for the deceased's parents, each of them receives one-sixth if he has a child, whether male or female, one or more. If he has no child and his two parents inherit from him, his mother receives one-third and his father the remainder. If the deceased has two or more siblings, male or female, his mother receives one-sixth, and the father receives the remainder, and the siblings receive nothing.﴾ This division of the estate takes place only after the deceased's bequest has been carried out, within the limit of one-third, or after his debts have been paid. ﴿Your fathers and your sons, you do not know which of them is nearer to you in benefit in this world and the Hereafter. So do not favor one of them over another. This is an obligation imposed on you by Allah. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of His creation, Wise in what He has legislated for them.﴾

And for you (men) is half of what your wives leave, if they have no child. If they have a child, then for you is a quarter of what they leave, after the fulfilment of any bequest they make that is permitted, or a debt they owe is settled. And for your wives (men) is a quarter of what you leave, if you have no child. If you have a child, then for them is an eighth of what you leave, after the fulfilment of any bequest you have made that is permitted, or the settlement of any debt you owe. And if a man or a woman leaves neither ascendant nor descendant as heir, and has a brother or a sister from the mother's side, then each of them receives a sixth. But if the brothers or sisters from the mother's side are more than that, they share in a third, divided equally among them, with no distinction between male and female. This is what Allah has prescribed for the brothers and sisters from the mother's side, which they take as their inheritance, after the fulfilment of the deceased's bequest if he made one, or the settlement of his debts, without harm to the heirs. This is the commandment of your Lord, a beneficial injunction for you. And Allah is All-Knowing of what benefits His creation, and Most Forbearing, who does not hasten to punish them.

The rulings that Allah has prescribed concerning orphans, women and inheritance are His laws, which show that they come from Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise. And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger in what He has prescribed for His servants of these rulings and others, He will admit him into gardens with many trees and palaces, beneath which rivers flow with their sweet waters, and they will abide therein, never leaving that bliss. That reward is the great triumph.

Whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger, by denying the rulings of Allah and transgressing what Allah has legislated for His servants, by altering them or by neglecting to act upon them, He will admit him into the Fire, remaining in it forever, and he will have a punishment that disgraces and humiliates him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 15:

And those of your women who commit unlawful sexual intercourse, then call to witness against them four men from among you, [O rulers and judges]. If they testify against them, then confine them to houses until death takes them or Allah ordains for them a way out of that.

The adulterers and adulteresses, the two who commit the immorality of unlawful intercourse (zina) — punish them both with beating, boycott, and rebuke. Then if they repent of what they did and amend themselves through righteous deeds that they send forward, then leave off harming them. It is derived from this verse and the one before it that men who commit immorality are harmed, while women are confined and harmed. Confinement ends in death, while harm ends in repentance and reform. This was at the beginning of Islam, and then it was abrogated (naskh) by what Allah and His Messenger legislated: stoning (rajm) for the one who is muhsan and the muhsanah, who are the two free adults of sound mind who have had intercourse within a valid marriage, and flogging with one hundred lashes, and banishment for one year for others. Indeed, Allah is ever Accepting of repentance from His servants who repent, Merciful to them.

Indeed, Allah accepts repentance only from those who commit evil deeds and sins out of ignorance (jahl) of their consequence and of the fact that they necessitate the wrath of Allah, and out of heedlessness and weakness of certainty. So every disobedient person toward Allah, whether he errs or does it deliberately, is ignorant in this respect, even if he knows the prohibition. Then they return to their Lord in repentance (inabah) and obedience before witnessing death. Those are the ones whose repentance Allah accepts. And Allah is All-Knowing of His creation, All-Wise in His management and decree.

Forgiveness is not accepted from those who persist in committing sins and do not return to their Lord until the agonies of death come upon them, so that one of them says, "Indeed, I have repented now." Nor is repentance accepted from those who die while disbelieving, denying the oneness of Allah and the message of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). For those who persist in sins until they die, and for those who disbelieve and die in disbelief, We have prepared a painful punishment.

O you who have believed, it is not lawful for you to inherit women against their will, [as you would inherit] property from your fathers' estates; nor should you restrain them, treating them as your possessions, by marrying them yourselves, preventing them from marrying, or giving them in marriage to others, when they are unwilling to accept any of this. Nor is it lawful for you to harm your wives, when you dislike them, so that they will give up part of the dower (mahr) and similar gifts you have given them, unless they commit a flagrant immorality such as adultery; in that case you may keep them, until they return what you have given them. Your living with your wives should be founded on honor and love, and on fulfilling the rights they are owed. If you dislike them for some worldly reason, then be patient, for it may be that you dislike something in which Allah has placed great good.

And if you desire to replace a wife with another, and you had given one of them a great amount of wealth as a dowry, then it is not lawful for you to take anything back from it. Would you take it by means of falsehood and manifest injustice?

**Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 4, verse 21:**

﴿And how could you take back from them that which you have given them as dower, while each of you has gone in unto the other, and they have taken from you a solemn covenant? Or keep them in honor or release them with kindness?﴾

Do not marry those women whom your fathers have married, except what has already passed of that in the time of ignorance; there is no blame for it. Indeed, marrying the wives of one's fathers is an ugly matter, extremely foul and abominable, and it is hateful, one whose doer Allah detests. Evil is the way and the course that you used to follow in your time of ignorance.

Allah has forbidden you to marry your mothers, which includes grandmothers on the father's side or the mother's side; and your daughters, which includes the daughters of your sons and daughters, however far down they go; and your sisters, whether full sisters, or sisters through the father or through the mother; and your paternal aunts, namely the sisters of your fathers and grandfathers; and your maternal aunts, namely the sisters of your mothers and grandmothers; and the daughters of your brothers, and the daughters of your sisters, which includes their children; and your nursing mothers who suckled you, and your foster sisters through nursing (the Messenger of Allah ﷺ forbade through nursing what is forbidden through blood relationship); and the mothers of your wives, whether or not you have consummated the marriage with your wives; and the daughters of your wives from other husbands, who are usually raised in your homes and under your care, and they are forbidden to you even if they are not in your guardianship; but this is on condition that you have consummated marriage with their mothers. If you have not consummated marriage with their mothers, and you have divorced them or they have died before consummation, then there is no sin upon you in marrying them. Allah has also forbidden you to marry the wives of your sons who are of your own loins, and those of your sons through nursing who have been attached to them; and this prohibition takes effect through the contract of marriage with her, whether or not the son has consummated the marriage. He has also forbidden you to combine in marriage, at one time, two sisters, whether by blood or by nursing, except what has already passed among you in the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam). It is likewise not permissible to combine a woman with her paternal aunt or her maternal aunt, as has come in the Sunnah. Indeed Allah is Forgiving to the sinners when they repent, and Merciful to them, so He does not burden them with what they cannot bear.

And [it is] forbidden for you to marry women who are already married, except those whom you have taken as captives in jihad, for it is lawful for you to marry them after purifying their wombs with one menstrual cycle. This is the decree of Allah upon you concerning the prohibition of marrying these women, and He has permitted for you the marrying of others besides them, [those] which Allah has made lawful for you, that you seek [them] with your wealth, guarding [yourselves] chastely, not committing what is unlawful. So whatever you have enjoyed of them through a valid marriage, give them their dowers which Allah has enjoined upon you. And there is no sin upon you in what you mutually agree upon [after the dower has been fixed], whether an increase or decrease in the dower, after the obligation has been established. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of the affairs of His servants, Wise in His legislation and His management.

Whoever does not have the means to pay the bridal gifts of free believing women, let him marry from among your believing slave girls who are in your possession. Allah, exalted is He, knows best the reality of your faith, for you are all from one soul and brothers in religion. So marry them with the consent of their masters, and give them their bridal gifts as agreed upon between you, with good will from you, while they are chaste, not openly committing unlawful intercourse, nor taking secret lovers. Then, if they marry and commit the immorality of fornication, they shall receive half the punishment prescribed for free women. The prescribed punishment for them is lashing, not stoning. That permission to marry slave women in the manner described earlier was granted only to one who fears falling into fornication himself and finds it hard to endure abstaining from intercourse. Yet patience in refraining from marrying slave women, while remaining chaste, is better and more virtuous. Allah is Forgiving to you and Merciful to you, for He permitted you to marry them when you are unable to marry free women.

God intends by these legislations to make clear to you the landmarks of His upright religion and His wise law, and to guide you to the ways of the prophets and the righteous before you regarding what is lawful and unlawful. He turns to you in forgiveness by bringing you back to acts of obedience, and He, glory be to Him, is All-Knowing of what sets right the affairs of His servants, and All-Wise in what He has legislated for you.
God desires to accept your repentance and to forgive your sins, while those who follow their own desires and pleasures want you to deviate tremendously from the religion.
God intends, by what He has legislated for you, ease and not hardship upon you, because you were created weak.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted according to His law, it is not lawful for you to consume one another's wealth unjustly, except that it be through trade in accordance with the law and lawful earning, by mutual consent among you. And do not kill one another, destroying yourselves by committing what Allah has forbidden and His acts of disobedience. Indeed, Allah has been Merciful to you in everything He has commanded you and forbidden you.

And whoever commits what Allah has forbidden, such as taking unlawful wealth through theft, usurpation and cheating, transgressing and going beyond the bounds of the Sharia, We will cast him into a Fire whose heat he will suffer; and that is easy for Allah.

If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden to commit, such as associating partners with Allah, disobeying your parents, killing a soul without right, and others besides these, O believers, We will remove from you the minor sins that fall below them, and We will admit you to an honourable entrance, which is Paradise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 32:

And do not wish for that by which Allah has made some of you excel over others, in endowments and provisions and other things. For Allah has allotted to men a portion of reward proportionate to their deeds, and has allotted to women a portion of what they have earned. And ask Allah, the Generous, the Bestower, and He will give you of His bounty instead of wishing. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of all things, and He knows best what is good for His servants in what He has apportioned to them.

For every one of you We have appointed heirs to inherit what the parents and the relatives leave behind, and those with whom you have made covenants by solemn oaths of support and of giving them a share of the inheritance, so give them their allotted portion. Inheritance by covenant (al-tahaluf) was at the beginning of Islam, then its ruling was abrogated (naskh) by the revelation of the verses on inheritance. Indeed, Allah is ever Knowing of everything you do, and He will recompense you for it.

Men are the guardians (qawwamun) over women, directing and caring for them, by virtue of the distinctive qualities of guardianship and preference that Allah has given them, and by what they give women of dowries and maintenance. So the righteous women among them are those who are upright upon the law of Allah, obedient to Allah the Exalted and to their husbands, guarding in their husbands' absence what is hidden from their husbands' knowledge, with what they have been entrusted with, by the protection and enabling grace of Allah. As for those from whom you fear haughtiness toward your obedience, admonish them with kind words; if kind words do not bear fruit with them, then forsake them in bed, and do not approach them; if the act of forsaking does not affect them, then strike them with a strike that causes no harm. Then if they obey you, do not seek a means against them, for Allah, the Most High, the Great, is their Protector, and He is the one who takes vengeance against whoever wrongs them and transgresses against them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 35:

And if you fear a breach between the two (spouses), O guardians of the couple, then send an arbiter from the husband's family and an arbiter from the wife's family, so that they may examine the matter and judge by what is in the interest of both of them. Through the sincere desire of the two arbiters for reconciliation, and their use of a gentle approach, Allah will bring about harmony between the spouses. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing; nothing about the affairs of His servants is hidden from Him, and He is Aware of what their souls conceal.

Worship Allah and submit to Him alone, and do not associate anything with Him in lordship or in worship. Be good to your parents and fulfil their rights, and the rights of your close relatives, the orphans whose fathers have died while they are below the age of maturity, the needy who do not possess what suffices them and meets their need, the neighbour who is near to you and the one who is far, the companion on a journey and at home, the traveller in need, and the slaves among your young men and young women. Indeed, Allah the Exalted does not love the arrogant among His servants, those who boast over people.

Those who withhold spending and giving from what Allah has provided them, who command others to be stingy, and who deny the blessings of Allah upon them, concealing His bounty and favor. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a humiliating punishment.

We have prepared this same punishment for those who spend their wealth out of show (riyā', ostentation) and for reputation (sum'ah, seeking to be heard of), and who do not believe in Allah, either in belief or in action, nor in the Day of Resurrection. These evil deeds are among the things to which Satan calls. Whoever has Satan as a constant companion, wretched is that companion and associate.

And what harm would befall them if they believed in Allah and the Last Day, both in belief and in deed, and spent out of what Allah had given them, seeking His reward and doing so sincerely? Allah, exalted is He, knows them and what they do, and He will call them to account for it.

Indeed, Allah does not wrong anyone by reducing any part of the reward of his deed by even the weight of an atom (dharrah). And if the weight of the atom is a good deed, then He, glory be to Him, multiplies it and increases it for its doer, and bestows upon him additional favour, giving him from His own presence a great reward, which is Paradise.

How then will it be with people on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah brings forth from every nation its messenger to bear witness against it for what it did, and brings you, O Messenger, to be a witness over your nation that you conveyed the message of your Lord?

On that Day, those who disbelieved in Allah and opposed the Messenger and did not obey him will wish that they were made equal with the earth, so that they would be turned to dust and would not be resurrected. And they will be unable to hide from Allah anything of what is in their selves, for Allah will have sealed their mouths, and their limbs will bear witness against them concerning what they used to do.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 43:

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not approach the prayer, nor stand up to it while intoxicated, until you can distinguish and know what you are saying (and this was before the definitive prohibition of wine in every state), and do not approach the prayer if you are in a state of major impurity (ḥadath akbar), nor approach its places, which are the mosques, except for those among you who are passing through from one door to another, until you purify yourselves by ghusl. And if you are in a state of illness in which you cannot use water, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the toilet (al-ghā'iṭ), or you have had intercourse with women, and you find no water for purification, then aim for clean earth (ṭayyiban) and wipe your faces and hands with it. Indeed, Allah is ever Most Pardoning, overlooking your sins and covering them for you.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the case of the Jews who were given a share of knowledge from what came to them in the Torah? They trade misguidance for guidance, and they abandon the proofs and evidences they possess, which indicate the truthfulness of the message of the Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ). They also wish for you, O believers who are guided, that you would deviate from the straight path, so that you would become astray like them.

God, glorified and exalted is He, knows better than you, O believers, the enmity of these Jews towards you. Sufficient is God as a Protector who takes charge of your affairs, and sufficient is He as a Helper who gives you victory over your enemies.

Among the Jews are a group who persistently distort the words of Allah and alter them from what they are, fabricating against Allah. They say to the Messenger (ﷺ): "We have heard your saying, and we disobey your command," and "Listen, may you not be made to hear," and they say: "Ra'ina sam'ak" (i.e., "Understand us, and let us understand you"), twisting their tongues with it, while they intend by it a supplication against him with ruin (ra'una), according to their language, and a slander against the religion of Islam. Had they said instead: "We have heard and we obey," in place of "and we disobey," and "Listen," without "unheard," and "Undhurna" (look at us) in place of "Ra'ina," it would have been better for them with Allah and more upright in speech. But Allah has expelled them from His mercy because of their disbelief and their denial of the prophethood of Muhammad (ﷺ), so they believe in the truth only with a little belief that does not benefit them.

O People of the Scripture, believe in and act upon what We have sent down, confirming what is with you of the Scriptures, before We efface faces and turn them backward, or curse them as We cursed the Sabbath-breakers, when they were forbidden to hunt on the Sabbath but did not desist. So Allah became angry with them, expelled them from His mercy, and the command of Allah is always carried out in every situation.

Indeed, Allah does not forgive, nor overlook, one who associates a partner with Him, ascribing to Him any of His creation, or who disbelieves in any form of the greatest disbelief (kufr). But He overlooks and pardons what is less than association (shirk) of sins, for whomever He wills of His servants. And whoever associates others with Allah has indeed fabricated a tremendous sin.

Did you not consider, O Messenger, the case of those who praise themselves and their deeds, describing them as pure and free from evil? Rather, it is Allah, the Exalted, alone who praises whom He wills of His servants, because of His knowledge of the reality of their deeds. And they will not be wronged even by an amount equal to the thread that is in the slit of a date-seed.

Look at them, O Messenger, in wonder at their affair: how they fabricate lies against Allah, when He is exalted above everything unfitting for Him? And this fabrication is sufficient as a great sin, revealing the corruption of their belief.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the case of those Jews who were given a share of knowledge, who believe in everything worshipped besides Allah, including idols and devils of mankind and jinn, with a belief that leads them to seek judgment from other than the law of Allah, and who say to those who disbelieve in Allah, may He be exalted, and in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ): "These disbelievers are more upright and more just in their way than those who believe"?

Those are the ones whose corruption has multiplied and whose misguidance has become general. Allah has expelled them from His mercy, and whoever Allah expels from His mercy, you will not find anyone to help him or to ward off from him the evil of the punishment.
Is it that they have a share in the kingdom? If they had been given it, they would not give anyone even a speck of it, not even the amount of the hollow in the back of a date-stone (the naqirah)?

Rather, do they envy Muhammad (ﷺ) for what Allah has given him of the blessing of prophethood and messengership, and envy his companions for the blessing of being guided to faith, affirming the message, following the Messenger, and being established in the land, and wish that this favour be removed from them? Indeed, We gave the progeny of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) before this the Scriptures, which Allah sent down to them, and that which was revealed to them, which was not a written book, and We gave them, in addition to that, a vast kingdom.

Among those who were given a share of knowledge are some who believed in the message of Muhammad (ﷺ) and acted according to his law, and others who turned away, did not respond to his call, and prevented people from following him. As for you, O deniers, the Fire of Hell, which is kindled with you, is sufficient for you.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 56:

Indeed, those who denied what Allah revealed of His signs, the revelation of His Book, His proofs and His evidences, We will surely cast into a Fire whose heat they will suffer. Whenever their skins are burned away, We will replace them with other skins, so that their punishment and pain may continue. Indeed, Allah is Almighty (ʿAzīz), nothing can resist Him, and He is All-Wise (Ḥakīm) in His management and His decree.

Those who have found tranquility in their hearts through faith in Allah, may He be exalted, and belief in the message of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and who have remained steadfast in obedience, We will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, through their palaces and trees. They will abide therein forever and will never leave them. For them therein are spouses purified by Allah from every defect, and We will admit them into dense, extended shade in Paradise.

God commands you to render the trusts (al-amanat) you have been entrusted with back to their rightful owners, so do not neglect them. He commands you to judge between people with justice and fairness when you judge between them. How excellent is that with which Allah admonishes you and guides you. Indeed, Allah is All-Hearing of your words, and All-Seeing of your deeds, having full knowledge of all of them.

O you who believe, obey Allah and His Messenger and act by His law. Respond to the commands of Allah, the Exalted, and do not disobey Him. Respond to the Messenger ﷺ in what he brought of the truth, and obey those in authority over you in what does not involve disobedience to Allah. If you dispute about anything among yourselves, then refer the matter concerning it back to the Book of Allah, the Exalted, and the Sunnah of His Messenger Muhammad ﷺ, if you truly believe in Allah and the Day of Reckoning. That referral to the Book and the Sunnah is better for you than disputing and speaking by personal opinion (ra'y), and better in outcome and final consequence.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the case of those hypocrites who claim to believe in what has been revealed to you, which is the Qur'an, and in what was revealed before you to the messengers? Yet they desire to seek judgment in their disputes from other than what Allah has legislated, which is falsehood, although they have been commanded to reject falsehood. And Satan wants to lead them far astray from the path of truth.

In this verse there is evidence that sincere faith requires submission to the law of Allah and judging by it in every matter. Whoever claims to be a believer yet chooses the judgment of the taghut (the transgressor, i.e., anything worshipped or obeyed beyond Allah) over the judgment of Allah, then he is lying in his claim.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 61:

And when these hypocrites are advised and told, "Come to what Allah has revealed, and to the Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), and his guidance," you see those who display faith while concealing disbelief turning away from you with aversion.

How then will those hypocrites fare when a calamity befalls them because of what their own hands have committed? Then they come to you, O Messenger, making excuses and swearing to you that they intended by those actions nothing but good and reconciliation between the disputing parties?

Those are the ones whom Allah knows to harbor hypocrisy (nifaq) in their hearts. So turn away from them, warn them against the evil of their state, and speak to them a word that is effective in them and restrains them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 64:

We did not send any messenger from among Our messengers except that he be obeyed, by the permission of Allah the Exalted and His decree. And if those who wronged themselves by committing evil deeds had come to you, O Messenger, during your lifetime, repenting and asking Allah to forgive them their sins, and you had asked forgiveness for them, they would have found Allah Accepting of repentance and Merciful.

God Most High swears by His noble Self that these people do not truly believe until they make you (ﷺ) the judge in whatever disputes arise between them during your lifetime, and bring their cases to your Sunnah after your death. Then they must not find in themselves any discomfort with the outcome of your judgment, and must submit completely to it. Thus, ruling by what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought, from the Book and the Sunnah, in every matter of life, is at the very core of faith, together with contentment and full submission.

If We had decreed for those hypocrites who seek judgment from the tyrant (al-ṭāghūt) that they kill one another or leave their homes, only a few of them would have carried it out. Yet if they had done what they were advised, it would have been beneficial for them and would have strengthened their faith. We would have given them from Our own presence a great reward in this world and the Hereafter, and We would have guided them and enabled them to follow the straight path of Allah.

If We had decreed for those hypocrites who seek judgment from the tyrant (al-ṭāghūt) that they kill one another or leave their homes, only a few of them would have carried it out. Yet if they had done what they were advised, it would have been beneficial for them and would have strengthened their faith. We would have given them from Our own presence a great reward in this world and the Hereafter, and We would have guided them and enabled them to follow the straight path of Allah.

If We had decreed for those hypocrites who seek judgment from the tyrant (al-ṭāghūt) that they kill one another or leave their homes, only a few of them would have carried it out. Yet if they had done what they were advised, it would have been beneficial for them and would have strengthened their faith. We would have given them from Our own presence a great reward in this world and the Hereafter, and We would have guided them and enabled them to follow the straight path of Allah.

Whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ), then those are the ones whose status and rank are great, and they will be in the company of those whom Allah has blessed with Paradise: the prophets, the siddiqun (the truthful ones) who have fully affirmed what the messengers brought, in belief, speech and action, the martyrs in the way of Allah, and the righteous among the believers. And excellent are these as companions in Paradise.

That great bounty comes from Allah alone. And Allah is sufficient as the All-Knowing, who knows the circumstances of His servants and who among them deserves the abundant reward for the righteous deeds he has performed.
O you who have believed, take your precaution: prepare yourselves against your enemy, and then go forth to meet them in groups, one group after another, or all together.

Indeed, among you is one who lingers behind, reluctant, from going out to meet the enemy, and who discourages others deliberately and persistently. So if a disaster befalls you, with death and defeat, he says, rejoicing: "God has blessed me, for I was not present with those who suffered what I would have disliked for myself," and he is delighted that he stayed behind from you.

"And if a bounty from Allah reaches you, and spoils of war, he will surely say—envious and full of regret, as though there had never been any affection between you and him outwardly—: 'Would that I had been with them, so that I might have attained what they attained of deliverance, victory, and spoils.'"

Let those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter and its reward fight in the cause of God, to support the religion of God and raise high His word. And whoever fights in the cause of God sincerely, and is killed or emerges victorious, We shall grant him a great reward.

Why is it that you do not fight in the cause of God, believers, to support His religion, and to support His oppressed servants, men, women and children, who are being persecuted, having no stratagem and no means except to cry out to their Lord, saying: "Our Lord, bring us out of this town" — meaning "Makkah" — "whose people have wronged themselves with disbelief and with harming the believers. And appoint for us from Yourself a protector who will take charge of our affairs, and a helper who will support us against the wrongdoers"?

The believers are those who are truthful in their faith, in belief and in deed, and who strive in the way of supporting the truth and its people. As for the disbelievers, they fight in the cause of transgression and corruption on the earth. So fight, O believers, against the people of disbelief and polytheism, who take Satan as their ally and obey his command. Indeed, the scheming of Satan against his followers is weak.

Have you not considered, O Messenger, the situation of those who were told, before permission to fight was given: "Restrain your hands from fighting your enemies among the polytheists, and fulfill what Allah has enjoined upon you of prayer and zakat." But when fighting was prescribed for them, behold, a group of them had changed their state: they began to fear people and dread them as much as, or more than, they feared Allah. They openly express the intensity of the fear that has overtaken them, saying: "Our Lord, why have You prescribed fighting for us? Would that You had delayed it for us to a near term," out of their desire for the fleeting enjoyments of worldly life. Say to them, O Messenger: "The enjoyment of this world is little, and the Hereafter, with what it contains, is greater and more lasting for whoever fears Allah, so he acts upon what he has been commanded and avoids what he has been forbidden." ﴿And your Lord does not wrong anyone the least bit, even if it were the weight of a thread inside the cleft of a date seed.﴾

Wherever you may be, death will overtake you, even if you are in fortresses built high and strong, far from the battlefield and fighting. And if good comes to them, they say, "This is from Allah," and if evil befalls them, they attribute it to the Messenger (ﷺ), out of ignorance and ill omen. But they do not realize that all of this is from Allah alone, by His decree and His destiny. Why, then, do they not come close to understanding any statement that is related to them?

Whatever good and blessing befalls you, O human, is from God alone, by His grace and kindness, and whatever harm and hardship befalls you is due to your own evil deeds and the sins and wrongs your hands have committed. And We have sent you, O Messenger, as a messenger to all mankind, to convey the message of your Lord, and God suffices as a witness to the truth of your message.

Whoever obeys the Messenger ﷺ and follows his guidance has indeed obeyed Allah, the Exalted, and complied with His command. As for whoever turns away from obedience to Allah and His Messenger, [know that] We did not send you, O Messenger, as a watcher over those who turn away, to guard their deeds and hold them accountable for them; their reckoning is upon Us.

These hypocrites, who are in the presence of the Messenger of God (ﷺ), display their obedience to the Messenger and to what he brought. But when they withdraw from him and leave his gathering, a group of them plot at night something other than what they had professed of obedience. They do not realize that God records what they plot, and He will repay them for it in full. So turn away from them, O Messenger, and do not concern yourself with them, for they will not harm you. Put your trust in God, and He is sufficient as a protector and helper for you.

Will these people not reflect upon the Qur'an and what it brings of truth, contemplating it and pondering over it, since it comes in a firmly ordered structure that makes clear that it is from Allah alone? Had it been from other than Allah, they would have found in it much inconsistency.

When there comes to them a matter of security or of fear, they spread it abroad. Had they referred it to the Messenger and to those in authority among them, those among them who investigate it would have known it. And were it not for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan, except for a few of you.

Note: the translation above is a rendering of the Qur'anic verse rather than of the commentary. Here is the full translation of the passage as requested:

When those whose faith has not yet settled in their hearts come upon a matter that should be kept secret, one bearing on security whose benefit returns to Islam and the Muslims, or on fear that leaves their hearts uneasy, they spread it and broadcast it among the people. Had these people referred what came to them to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and to the people of knowledge and understanding, those among them capable of deduction would have known the true meaning of it. And had it not been for Allah's favour upon you and His mercy, you would have followed Satan and his whisperings, except for a few of you.

Fight, O Prophet, in the way of Allah and for the elevation of His word. You are not held responsible for the actions of others, nor will you be called to account for them. Urge the believers to fight and to strive, and encourage them to do so, so that perhaps Allah will restrain, through you and them, the might and violence of the disbelievers. And Allah, exalted is He, is mightier in strength and more severe in punishment against the disbelievers.

Whoever strives to obtain good for another, he will have a share of the reward for his intercession, and whoever strives to bring harm to another, he will have a share of the burden and sin. And Allah is ever Witness over all things and Guardian over them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 86:

When a Muslim greets you with salam, respond with something better than his greeting, in words and in warmth, or at least return it in the same manner. Each will receive its reward and recompense. Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, is ever Recompenser of everything.110

Allah, who alone is the One deserving worship by all creation, will surely gather you on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt, for reckoning and recompense. And none is more truthful in speech than Allah in what He reports.

Why, then, do you (believers) differ about the hypocrites, becoming two factions: one faction saying they should be fought, and another not saying so? Allah the Exalted has caused them to fall into disbelief and misguidance because of their evil deeds. Do you wish to guide those whom Allah has turned away from His religion? And whoever Allah has forsaken, so that he does not follow His religion and what He commanded him, there is no path for him to guidance.

The hypocrites wish that you, O believers, would disbelieve just as they have disbelieved, so that you would be equal to them in disbelief. So do not take any of them as close friends until they emigrate in the cause of Allah as proof of the sincerity of their faith. But if they turn away from what they are called to, then seize them wherever you find them and kill them, and do not take from among them any ally apart from Allah, nor any helper whom you seek help from.

But those who join a people between whom and you there is a treaty and covenant, [then do not fight them]; and likewise those who come to you with hearts constricted, reluctant to fight you or to fight their own people. Had God willed, He would have given them power over you, and they would have fought you alongside your enemies from among the polytheists. But God turned them away from you by His grace and His power. So if they withdraw from you and do not fight you, and submit to you in peace, then you have no way against them to fight them.

You will find others who wish to be safe from both sides: they show you faith, and they show their own disbelieving people disbelief. Whenever they are returned to the place of disbelief and its people, they fall into the worst of states. So if these do not withdraw from you, offer you full surrender, and restrain themselves from fighting you, then seize them with force and kill them wherever you find them. Those who have gone so far in this evil course as to set themselves apart from everyone else, these are the ones for whom We have given you a clear proof to kill and to take them captive.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 92:

It is not permissible for a believer to attack his believing brother and kill him without right, except that it happens from him by way of error (khata'), in which there is no intent (amd). Whoever commits that error must free a believing slave (raqabah mu'minah) and hand over a fixed blood-money (diyah) to the heirs of the slain, unless they waive it as charity and pardon him. If the slain person was from a people of disbelievers who are enemies of the believers, while he himself was a believer in Allah, the Exalted, and in what He sent down of truth upon His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), then his killer must free a believing slave, [and no diyah is due]. If he was from a people between you and whom there is a covenant and a pact, then his killer must pay a diyah handed over to his heirs and free a believing slave. Whoever does not find the means to free a believing slave must fast two consecutive months, in order that Allah may turn to him in forgiveness. Allah was ever All-Knowing of the true state of His servants, All-Wise in what He has legislated for them.

Whoever deliberately kills a believer, without right, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein forever, along with the wrath of God upon him and His casting him out of His mercy, if He recompenses him for his sin. God has prepared for him a terrible punishment, because of this grave crime he committed. But God, glorified is He, pardons and bestows favor upon the people of faith, so He does not recompense them with eternal abiding in Hell.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted in accordance with His law: when you go forth in the land fighting in the cause of Allah, then verify carefully what you undertake and what you refrain from, and do not say of one who shows some sign of Islam and does not fight you, "You are not a believer," for it is possible that he is a believer who conceals his faith, while you seek thereby the goods of the worldly life. Yet with Allah is abundant bounty and provision, which will suffice you. Thus you were at the beginning of Islam, concealing your faith from your people among the polytheists, and then Allah bestowed His favor upon you and strengthened you with faith and power. So be certain and well-informed in your affairs. Indeed, Allah is All-Knowing of all your deeds, aware of the subtleties of your affairs, and He will recompense you for them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 95:

Those believers who stay behind from jihad in the cause of Allah, other than those who have valid excuses among them, are not equal to those who strive in the cause of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred the strivers over those who stay behind, and has raised their rank by a high degree in Paradise. Allah has promised every one of them, both those who strive with their wealth and their lives and those who stay behind due to valid excuses, the Garden, in return for what they gave and sacrificed in the cause of the truth. Allah has preferred the strivers over those who stay behind with a great reward.

This great reward, lofty ranks in the Gardens from Allah, the Exalted, is for His chosen servants who strive in His cause, along with forgiveness for their sins and vast mercy, in which they will take delight. Allah is ever Forgiving to whoever repents to Him and turns back to Him, and Merciful to those who obey Him, the strivers in His cause.

Indeed, those whom the angels take in death while they have wronged themselves by remaining in the land of disbelief and abandoning the emigration (hijrah), the angels will say to them in reproach: "In what state were you regarding your religion?" They will say: "We were weak in our land, unable to repel oppression and subjugation from ourselves." The angels will say to them in reproach: "Was not the earth of Allah spacious, so that you could have emigrated from your land to another land where you would be safe in your religion?" Those, their abode is Hellfire, and wretched is this destination and return.

Those who are truly helpless among men, women, and children, who cannot ward off oppression and injustice from themselves and do not know a way to free them from the hardship they are in, are excused from that fate.

These weak ones are the ones for whom forgiveness from Allah, the Exalted, is hoped, because of His knowledge of the reality of their condition. And Allah is ever Most Forgiving, overlooking their misdeeds and concealing them from others.

Whoever leaves the land of polytheism for the land of Islam, fleeing with his religion, hoping for the bounty of his Lord and intending to support his religion, will find in the earth a place of refuge and a place to move to, where he will enjoy what becomes a cause of his strength and the humiliation of his enemies, along with abundance in his provision and livelihood. And whoever leaves his home intending to support the religion of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ) and to raise the word of Allah, and then death overtakes him before he reaches his goal, then his reward for his deed is certainly established with Allah, as a bounty and a kindness from Him. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful toward His servants.

When you travel through the land, O believers, there is no blame on you for shortening the prayer if you fear that the disbelievers may attack you while you pray. The majority of the journeys of the Muslims in the early days of Islam were fraught with danger, and shortening the prayer is a concession (rukhsah) for travel, whether in safety or in fear. Indeed, the disbelievers openly show their enmity toward you, so be wary of them.

When you, O Prophet, are among them in the battlefield and you intend to lead them in prayer, let one group of them stand with you in prayer, and let them take up their weapons. When those [in the first group] prostrate, let the other group be behind you, facing your enemy. Then let the first group, who have not yet prayed, come and pray with you one rak'ah, and then they should complete their second rak'ah by themselves, and then they should give the salam. Then the other group, who have not yet begun the prayer, should come and pray with you their first rak'ah, then they should complete their second rak'ah by themselves. And let them be cautious of their enemy and take up their weapons. Those who disbelieve in the religion of Allah wish that you would be heedless of your weapons and your provisions, so that they might attack you in a single assault and finish you off. And there is no blame upon you if you are troubled by rain or are ill, that you put down your weapons, but take your precaution. Indeed, Allah has prepared for those who deny His religion a humiliating punishment that will disgrace them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 103:

So when you have finished the prayer, remember God in all your circumstances, standing, sitting, and lying on your sides. Then, when fear has passed, perform the prayer in full, and do not neglect it, for it is an obligation at times prescribed in the Sharia.

Do not weaken in pursuing your enemy and fighting them. If you suffer pain from the fighting and its effects, then your enemies also suffer from it, even more intensely, yet they do not cease fighting you. You are more deserving of this than they are, because of what you hope for from reward, victory and support, which they do not hope for. And Allah is All-Knowing of all your circumstances, All-Wise in His command and His arrangement.

We have sent down to you, O Messenger, the Qur'an containing the truth, so that you may judge between people by what Allah has shown you and made you understand. So do not be a defender for those who betray themselves by concealing the truth, by what they have presented to you of statements contrary to reality.
And ask Allah for forgiveness in all your circumstances. Indeed, Allah is ever Forgiving to those who hope for His bounty and the attainment of His forgiveness, and Merciful toward them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 107:

And do not defend those who betray themselves through disobedience to Allah. Indeed, Allah, glorified is He, does not love one whose treachery is great and whose sin is abundant.

They hide themselves from people, fearing that their evil deeds will be discovered by them, yet they do not hide themselves from Allah, nor are they ashamed before Him. He, exalted is His majesty, is with them by His knowledge, watching over them when they plot at night what He does not approve of in speech. Allah, may He be exalted, encompasses all their words and deeds; nothing of them is hidden from Him.

You, believers, have argued on behalf of these people who betrayed themselves in this worldly life. But who will argue on their behalf before God on the Day of Resurrection and Reckoning? And who will be a guardian over these betrayers on the Day of Resurrection?

Whoever commits an evil deed, ugly in itself, or wrongs himself by doing what contradicts the command of Allah and His law, then turns back to Allah in regret for what he did, hoping for His forgiveness and the covering of his sin, will find Allah Forgiving toward him and Merciful to him.
Whoever deliberately commits a sin only harms himself, and Allah, exalted is He, is All-Knowing of the true reality of His servants' affairs, and All-Wise in what He decrees among His creatures.

And whoever commits a sin unintentionally, or deliberately commits a wrong and then throws the blame for what he committed onto an innocent person who had no part in it, has borne a slander and a manifest sin.

Had it not been for Allah's grace upon you, O Messenger, and His mercy toward you through the blessing of prophethood, by which He protected you through His guidance in what He revealed to you, a group of those who betray themselves would have resolved to lead you astray from the path of truth. Yet they lead astray none but themselves, and they cannot harm you, because Allah protects you. And Allah sent down to you the Qur'an and the Sunnah that explains it, and guided you to knowledge of what you did not know before. The favor Allah has bestowed upon you is indeed a great thing.

There is no good in much of the secret talk among people, except for talk that calls to giving charity, to a kind word, or to reconciling between people. Whoever does these things seeking the pleasure of Allah, hoping for His reward, We will grant him a great and abundant reward.

And whoever opposes the Messenger (ﷺ) after the truth has become clear to him, and follows a path other than the path of the believers and what they hold to of the truth, We will leave him to what he has turned to, and We will not guide him to good, and We will admit him into the Fire of Hell, where he will endure its heat. And wretched is this destination and final return.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 116:

Indeed, Allah does not forgive that He be associated with in worship, and He forgives what is less than that of sins to whom He wills of His servants. And whoever sets up for Allah, the One, the Unique, a partner from among His creation, has strayed far from the truth.

The polytheists worship, besides Allah the Exalted, only idols that can neither benefit nor harm, and they worship none but a rebellious devil, rebellious against Allah, who has reached a great extent in corruption and in causing corruption.
Allah has expelled him from His mercy. And Satan said: "I will surely take from Your servants a specified portion [to lead astray]."

Surely I will lead astray those among them who follow me from the truth, and I will feed them with false hopes, and I will command them to slit the ears of cattle and split them, because of what I make attractive to them of falsehood; and I will command them to alter the creation of God in its natural disposition (fitrah) and the form in which people were created. Whoever obeys Satan and takes him as a helper instead of God, the Mighty, the Powerful, has surely lost with a clear loss.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 120:

Satan promises his followers false promises, and entices them with vain, deceptive wishes. What he promises them is nothing but a delusion with no truth to it and no proof for it.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 121:

﴿Those, their final abode is Hell, and they will find no escape from it and no refuge.﴾

Those who were true in their faith in Allah, the Exalted, and followed their faith with righteous deeds, Allah will admit them, by His grace, into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. It is a promise from Allah, the Exalted, who never breaks His promise. And none is more truthful than Allah in His word and His promise.

This grand reward is not attained through wishful thinking, neither the wishes you entertain, O Muslims, nor the wishes of the People of the Book, the Jews and the Christians. Rather, it is attained through sincere faith in Allah, exalted is He, and through doing righteous deeds that please Him. Whoever does an evil deed will be recompensed for it, and he will find besides Allah no protector (walī) who takes charge of his affairs and his situation, nor any helper (naṣīr) who supports him and averts from him the evil of the punishment.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 124:

Whoever does righteous deeds, whether male or female, while being a believer in Allah, the Exalted, and in what He has sent down of truth, those will enter Paradise, the abode of lasting bliss, and they will not be wronged in the reward of their deeds even by an amount as small as the speck in the hollow of a date-stone.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 125:

No one is better in religion than one who submits his heart and all his limbs to Allah alone, who is a doer of good in his words and deeds, obeying the command of his Lord, and who follows the religion and law of Ibrahim (Abraham), turning away from corrupt beliefs and false laws. Allah chose Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and took him as a khalil (intimate friend) above all of His creation. And in this verse is an affirmation of the attribute of khullah (intimate friendship) for Allah, Exalted is He, which is the highest rank of love and selection.

To Allah belongs everything in this universe of creatures; they are His alone, owned by Him, exalted is He. And Allah has encompassed all things, nothing among the affairs of His creation is hidden from Him.

People are asking you, O Prophet, to clarify for them what they have found difficult to understand regarding matters of women and their rulings. Say: God makes clear to you their affairs, and also what is recited to you in the Book concerning the orphan women whom you do not give what God has prescribed for them of dowry and inheritance, and other rights, while you desire to marry them, or you turn away from marrying them. God makes clear to you the matter of the weak among the young, and the obligation to stand up for orphans, those whose fathers have died while they are below the age of puberty, with justice, and to refrain from oppressing them in their rights. And whatever good you do, indeed God is ever Knowing of it, nothing of it or of anything else is hidden from Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 128:

If a woman fears ill-treatment or aversion from her husband, through his haughtiness and disdain toward her, or his turning away from her, then there is no sin upon them if they reconcile between themselves with whatever their souls find agreeable regarding the division of time or maintenance. Reconciliation is better and more excellent. Souls have been created with greed and stinginess, as though stinginess is always present with them and never leaves them. And if you do good in your treatment of your wives and fear Allah concerning them, then indeed Allah is ever aware of what you do of that and other than it, nothing is hidden from Him, and He will reward you for it.

You will never be able to achieve perfect justice among wives in affection and inclination of the heart, no matter how hard you strive for it, O men. So do not turn away completely from the one you do not desire, leaving her like a woman who is neither married nor divorced, and thus incur sin. And if you set your affairs right, by being just in your division [of time and provision] among your wives, and you watch over yourselves before God and fear Him regarding them, then indeed God is Forgiving toward His servants and Merciful to them.

If a separation takes place between a man and his wife, then Allah, exalted is He, will make each of them independent through His bounty and His vastness. For He, glorified and exalted, is abundant in grace and favor, and wise in what He decrees among His servants.

This is the commentary (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 131 of the King Fahd Complex.

Translation:

﴿To Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. And We have certainly enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you, and upon you as well, to fear Allah.﴾ We have enjoined upon those who were given the Scripture before you, from the Jews and the Christians, and We have enjoined upon you likewise, O Ummah of Muhammad (ﷺ), to be mindful of Allah the Exalted, to stand by His command, and to avoid His prohibitions. We have also made clear to you that if you deny the oneness of Allah the Exalted and His law, then He, glory be to Him, is without need of you, because to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is on the earth. And Allah is ever Self-Sufficient, free of need from His creation, Praiseworthy in His attributes and His actions.
To Allah belongs the dominion of all the creatures in this universe. He, glorified is He, suffices as the One who manages the affairs of His creation and preserves them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 133:

﴿If He wills, He can do away with you, O mankind, and bring others in your place. And Allah is ever competent to do that.﴾

Whoever among you, O people, desires the reward of this world and turns away from the Hereafter, then with Allah alone is the reward of this world and the Hereafter. So let him seek from Allah alone the good of both the world and the Hereafter, for it is He who possesses them both. And Allah is All-Hearing of the words of His servants, All-Seeing of their intentions and their deeds, and He will recompense them for that.

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: be steadfast in upholding justice, bearing witness for the sake of Allah, even if it is against yourselves, or against your parents and relatives, whatever the状况 of the one testified against, whether rich or poor. For Allah is more entitled to both of them than you are, and He knows best what is good for them. So do not let desire and partisanship lead you to abandon justice. And if you distort the testimony with your tongues, so that you give it in other than its true form, or if you turn away from it by refraining from giving it or by concealing it, then indeed Allah is ever Knowing of the subtleties of your deeds, and He will recompense you for them.

O you who have believed, believe in Allah and His Messenger, and in the Book that He sent down upon His Messenger, and in the Scripture that He sent down before. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the Last Day, has certainly strayed far astray.

Translation of the commentary:

O you who have believed (صَدَّقوا الله ورسوله وعملوا بشرعه): persevere in what you are upon of firm affirmation of Allah, the Exalted, and of His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and in obeying the two of them, and in the Qur'an which He sent down to him, and in all the Books which Allah sent down to the Messengers. And whoever disbelieves in Allah, the Exalted, and His honored angels, and His Books which He sent down for the guidance of His creation, and His Messengers whom He chose to convey His message, and the Last Day on which people will rise after their death for presentation and reckoning, then he has indeed left the religion and strayed a great straying from the path of truth.

Indeed, those who believed, then disbelieved, then believed again, then disbelieved once more, and then persisted in their disbelief and continued upon it, Allah will not forgive them, nor will He guide them to any path of guidance by which they would be saved from an evil end.
Tell the hypocrites, O Messenger, (those who show faith while concealing disbelief) that there is a painful punishment awaiting them.

Those who take the disbelievers as allies, making them their helpers, and abandon allegiance to the believers, not desiring their companionship. Do they seek support and protection from the disbelievers? They do not possess that; all support, honour and power belong to Allah alone.

And your Lord has already sent down to you, O believers, in His Book that when you hear the disbelief in the signs of Allah and their mockery, you should not sit with the disbelievers and the mockers, unless they turn to a conversation other than the talk of disbelief and mockery of the signs of Allah. Indeed, if you sit with them while they are in the state they are in, then you are like them, because you have approved of their disbelief and their mockery, and whoever approves of a sin is like one who commits it. Indeed, Allah, exalted is He, will gather the hypocrites and the disbelievers all together in the Fire of Hell, where they will suffer the worst torment.

The hypocrites are those who wait to see what befalls you, O believers, of trials and war. If God grants you victory and bestows on you His favour, by granting you triumph over your enemy and spoils of war, they say to you: "Were we not with you, supporting you?" And if the deniers of this religion obtain some measure of victory and spoils, they say to them: "Did we not help you with what we had already done for you, and protect you from the believers?" God, the Exalted, will judge between you and them on the Day of Resurrection. God will never grant the disbelievers a way to overcome His righteous servants, and the final outcome belongs to the God-fearing, both in this world and in the Hereafter.

The way of these hypocrites is deceiving Allah, the Exalted, by displaying faith and concealing disbelief, thinking that this is hidden from Allah. But in reality, Allah deceives them and will repay them in kind for their deeds. When these hypocrites stand to perform the prayer, they stand up to it lazily, intending by their prayer showing-off (riya') and seeking to be seen and heard (sum'ah), and they do not remember Allah except a little.

The hypocrites are characterized by wavering, bewilderment, and instability; they settle on no single state. They are neither with the believers nor with the disbelievers. And whomever Allah causes to go astray, turning his heart away from faith in Him and from holding fast to His guidance, you will never find for him a path to guidance and certainty.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not take as allies the disbelievers who deny the religion of Allah, leaving off allying with and loving the believers. Do you want to give Allah a clear proof against yourselves, by your befriending your enemies, that you are not truthful in your faith?

The commentary on surah 4, verse 145:

Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest levels of the Fire on the Day of Resurrection, and you, O Messenger, will not find for them any helper who can ward off from them the evil of this fate.

Except for those who repent, make amends, hold fast to Allah's religion, and devote their worship sincerely to Him. Such people are with the believers in this world and the Hereafter, and Allah will surely give the believers a great reward.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 147:

What would Allah gain by punishing you if you give thanks and believe in Allah and His Messenger? Allah is Most High, self-sufficient, free of need from anything other than Himself, and He punishes people only for their sins. Allah is Appreciative of His servants for their obedience to Him, and He is All-Knowing of everything.

God does not like anyone to speak evil openly, but the wronged person is permitted to mention his wrongdoer for the evil in him, so that he may make his injustice known. And God is All-Hearing of what you say openly, All-Knowing of what you conceal of that.

God (exalted is He) encourages forgiveness, and paves the way for it by explaining that the believer either displays good or conceals it. Likewise, with wrongdoing: one may either make it known when taking redress against the wrongdoer, or pardon and overlook it, and pardoning is better, for among God's attributes (exalted is He) is that He pardons His servants while He has power over them.

Indeed, those who disbelieve in Allah and His messengers, from among the Jews and the Christians, and who wish to make a distinction between Allah and His messengers, by believing in Allah while denying His messengers whom He sent to His creation, or by acknowledging the truthfulness of some messengers but not others, and claiming that some of them had fabricated lies against their Lord, and who wish to adopt a path to the misguidance that they have invented and the innovation that they have originated.
Those are the people of certain disbelief, about which there is no doubt. And We have prepared for the disbelievers a punishment that will disgrace them and humiliate them.

Those who affirmed the oneness of God, acknowledged the prophethood of all His messengers, did not make any distinction between any of them, and acted in accordance with the law of God—those, He will surely give them their reward and recompense for their faith in Him and His messengers. And God is ever Forgiving toward His servants, Merciful to them.

The People of the Book ask you, O Messenger, for a miracle like the miracle of Musa (Moses), one that would attest to your truthfulness: that a written scripture be sent down to them from Allah, just as Musa brought the tablets from Allah. So do not be surprised, O Messenger, for their forefathers asked Musa (peace be upon him) for something even greater. They asked him to show them Allah openly, and so the destructive punishment seized them, because of their wronging of themselves in asking for something that was not their right. After Allah revived them following the stroke, and after they had witnessed the clear signs at the hand of Musa, which decisively negate polytheism, they worshipped the calf instead of Allah. Yet We pardoned them for worshipping the calf because of their repentance, and We gave Musa a mighty proof that confirms the truthfulness of his prophethood.
