The commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 156:

And so We cursed them because of their disbelief and their slander against Maryam, by what they attributed to her of fornication, while she was innocent of it.

Because of their saying, in mockery and derision: "Indeed, we killed the Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, the Messenger of Allah." But they did not kill him, nor did they crucify him; rather, it was made to appear so to them, and they crucified a man resembling him, thinking that he was Jesus. Those who claimed to have killed him from among the Jews, and likewise those among the Christians who handed him over to them, are all in doubt and confusion. They have no knowledge in this, except following conjecture, and they did not kill him with certainty, but rather in doubt and mere supposition.
Nay, Allah raised Jesus up to Himself, body and soul, alive, and delivered him from those who disbelieved. And Allah is Almighty in His dominion, All-Wise in His management and decree.

There will not remain any of the People of the Book after the descent of Jesus at the end of time who does not believe in him before his death, peace be upon him. On the Day of Resurrection, Jesus, peace be upon him, will be a witness against those who denied him, by affirming their denial, and a witness for those who believed in him, by affirming their belief.

Because of the wrongdoing of the Jews, through the grave sins they committed, Allah forbade them some good foods that had been lawful for them, and because of their turning themselves and others away from the upright religion of Allah.

And because of their consuming of usury (riba), which they had been forbidden, and their taking of people's wealth without right, and We have prepared for the disbelievers in Allah and His Messenger from among these Jews a painful punishment in the Hereafter.

But those firmly grounded in knowledge among them, and the believers, believe in what has been sent down to you, [O Messenger], which is the Qur'an, and in what was sent down before you, such as the Torah and the Gospel. They establish the prayer at its appointed times, give the zakat (obligatory charity) on their wealth, and believe in Allah and in the Resurrection and the Recompense. Those—Allah will give them a great reward, which is Paradise.

We have revealed to you, O Messenger, the conveying of the message, just as We revealed to Nuh (Noah) and the prophets after him. We revealed to Ibrahim (Abraham), Isma'il (Ishmael), Ishaq (Isaac), and Ya'qub (Jacob), and the Asbat (the tribes), who are the prophets from the descendants of Ya'qub, who were among the twelve tribes of the Children of Israel, and to 'Isa (Jesus), Ayyub (Job), Yunus (Jonah), Harun (Aaron), and Sulayman (Solomon). And We gave Dawud (David) the Zabur (Psalms), which is a book and written scriptures.

We sent messengers whom We have related to you in the Qur'an before this verse, and messengers whom We have not related to you, for a wisdom We intended. And Allah spoke to Musa (Moses) directly, [an act of] honoring him with this attribute. In this noble verse is the affirmation of the attribute of speech for Allah, may He be exalted, as befits His majesty, and that He, glorified is He, spoke to His Prophet Musa, peace be upon him, in reality, without intermediary.

I sent messengers to My creation as bearers of good news of My reward and as warners of My punishment, so that people would have no argument to offer as an excuse after the sending of the messengers. And Allah is Almighty in His dominion, All-Wise in His management.

If the Jews and others deny you, O Messenger, then Allah bears witness for you that you are His Messenger, to whom He sent down the Great Qur'an. He sent it down with His knowledge, and the angels likewise bear witness to the truth of what was revealed to you. And the testimony of Allah alone is sufficient.
Indeed, those who denied your prophethood and barred people from Islam have strayed far from the path of truth.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 168:

Indeed, those who disbelieved in Allah and His Messenger, and who wronged themselves by persisting in disbelief, Allah would not forgive their sins, nor would He guide them to a path that would save them.
Except the path of Hell, remaining therein forever. And that is ever easy for Allah, so nothing can overpower Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 170:

O mankind, there has come to you our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ) with the religion of truth from your Lord, with Islam. So believe him and follow him, for belief in him is better for you. But if you persist in your disbelief, then indeed Allah is free of need of you and of your faith, because to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth. And Allah has always been All-Knowing of your statements and your deeds, All-Wise in His legislation and His command. Since the heavens and the earth have submitted to Allah, the Exalted, in their existence and decree, in the submission of all His dominion, it is more fitting for you to believe in Allah and in His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and in the Qur'an that He sent down to him, and to submit to that in legislation as well, so that the whole universe may be subject to Allah in decree and in law. In the verse is evidence for the universality of the mission of the Prophet of Allah and His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

O People of the Gospel, do not exceed the bounds of the true belief in your religion, and do not say about God except the truth: so do not associate with Him a consort or a son. The Messiah, Jesus son of Mary, is only the Messenger of God, whom God sent with the truth, and He created him by the Word that He sent with Gabriel to Mary, namely His saying "Be!" and he was. He was also a breath from God, which Gabriel blew by the command of his Lord. So believe that God is One, submit to Him, and believe His messengers in what they have brought you from God, and act upon it; and do not make Jesus and his mother partners with God. Desist from this claim; it is better for you than what you are upon. Indeed God is one God, glory be to Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, so how could He have a consort or a son from among them? And God suffices as a Guardian over the management of His creation and the disposition of their affairs, so put your trust in Him alone, for He is sufficient for you.

The Messiah will never disdain or refuse to be a servant of Allah, and neither will the angels who are brought near (to Allah) disdain to acknowledge their servitude to Allah, the Exalted. Whoever disdains submission and obedience and becomes arrogant, He will gather them all to Him on the Day of Resurrection, judge between them with His just judgment, and recompense each one according to what he deserves.

As for those who believed in Allah, in belief, speech and action, and remained steadfast upon His law, He will give them in full the reward of their deeds and will increase them from His bounty. As for those who refused to obey Allah and were arrogant against humbling themselves before Him, He will punish them with a painful punishment, and they will find for themselves no protector who can save them from His punishment, nor any helper who can defend them besides Allah.

O people, there has come to you a proof from your Lord, and it is our Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ), and what he brought of clear signs and decisive proofs, the greatest of which is the Noble Qur'an, which testifies to the truthfulness of his prophethood and his final message. And We have sent down to you the Qur'an as guidance and a clear light.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 175:

As for those who truly believed in Allah, in belief, speech and action, and held fast to the light that was sent down to them, He will admit them into Paradise out of His mercy and grace, and He will guide them to the straight path that leads to the gardens of Paradise.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 4, verse 176:

They ask you, O Prophet, about the ruling on the inheritance of kalala (the estate of one who dies leaving neither children nor parents). Say: "Allah explains to you the ruling concerning it: If a man dies leaving no child and no parent, and he has a sister (from both father and mother, or from the father only), then she receives half of his estate, and her brother inherits all of her property if she dies leaving no child and no parent, whether he is a full brother or a brother from the father only. If the one who dies as a kalala leaves two sisters, then they receive two-thirds of what he left. And if male siblings from the father's side combine with female siblings, the male receives the equivalent of the share of two females among his sisters." Allah explains to you the distribution of inheritances and the ruling on kalala, lest you go astray from the truth regarding matters of inheritance. And Allah is the Knower of the outcomes of affairs, and of what good there is in them for His servants.
